newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat higher after fund rolls out March longs.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat higher after fund rolls out March longs.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures were higher at the midsession after a commission house tied to large fund interests rolled its March longs out to the May, traders said.
The commission house, Rosenthal Collins, bear-spread two million May/March bushels at 28 to 29 cents, traders said. On Tuesday, Rosenthal did four million of the same spread.

"The big story in Kansas City is the collapse of the March/May spread. It's traded into 25/26 (cents per bushel) from about 29 cents -- mostly on fund length rolling into May," a KCBT floor broker said.
At 1137 CST, KCBT wheat was 1-1/2 to four cents per bushel higher, with March up 1-1/2 cents at $4.20-1/4 a bushel. May was up three cents at $3.94.
Traders said the July contract appeared to have shrugged off the early bearish tone that was brought on by the arrival of needed rains in HRW growing regions in Texas and Oklahoma.
Other players apart from Rosenthal, included Term Commodities, which bought 1.2 million Sept 1997 bushels, traders said. CIS bull-spread nearly one million March/May at 27 to 29 cents, sources said.
